Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens & host comparisons

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion. Quick recap and the asks I promised to follow up on: 

1) Your volume profile (as discussed):
   - Steady-state: ~100M tokens / month
   - Event-driven peak: up to ~250M tokens in high traffic weeks
   - Embedding usage: ~10% of token volume, higher latency tolerance

2) Budget / target price horizon: you mentioned a target of mid-single digits $/1M tokens if we can meet quality/SLOs and contract term (12mo). You asked for a concrete benchmarking callout vs OpenAI / Anthropic / common open-hosts.

3) Next steps from Redwood: I'll attach a short benchmarking summary (assumptions, token definition, inference vs embedding costs) and a draft mutual action plan to get procurement/engineering aligned. Can you:
   - Confirm the 12mo commit range for pricing (rough number is fine)
   - Share the procurement contact / PO process (I cc'd procurement@brightleaf.ai if helpful)

Attachment: BrightLeaf_Q1_usage_estimate.csv (you shared today) — I pulled the numbers into our template.

Initial thought on where Redwood can land given your profile: with a 12mo committed tier + predictable throughput, we can propose something materially below public host list prices by leaning on Dedicated capacity and workload optimizations (KV caching + quantization). I'll convert these into a clear $/1M tokens table and send back by EOD tomorrow.

Best,

- Committed volume: our best estimate for a 12mo commit window is ~1.2 billion tokens (that aggregates expected rollout across three product surfaces).
- Budget: engineering/product are targeting $5–$7 / 1M tokens as an aspirational procurement number; we understand that's aggressive versus public hosts but worth exploring with a committed agreement.
- SLOs: 95th p95 latency target ~220ms for text-gen, embeddings can be relaxed. Will need token-level billing export for monthly reconciliation.

Can you include a short table that compares: public-host list price (OpenAI/Anthropic), typical open-host managed price, and Redwood's committed-dedicated vs private/VPC options — all expressed as $/1M tokens with the assumptions used.

If you can get that to us tomorrow, procurement and I will review and try to align internally. We can schedule a follow-up with procurement and infrastructure leads next week.

Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M tokens & host comparisons — Redwood benchmark (attached)

Appended the benchmarking PDF and a short set of assumptions — file: redwood-target-price-benchmarks-1Mtokens.pdf (attached). Key highlights and an initial commitment-tier proposal below.

Benchmark assumptions (short):
- Token definition: raw model input+output tokens using common tokenizer (we align to OpenAI token counting for apples-to-apples)
- Mix: 90% text-gen (low context ~512 tokens), 10% embeddings
- SLOs: p95 latency targets as discussed
- Cost levers included: quantization (4/8-bit where applicable), KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, batching on Dedicated pools

Initial $/1M token table (illustrative, excludes marginal infra pass-throughs like private network transit):
- OpenAI (public API list price reference): ~$20 / 1M tokens (public-gen models)
- Anthropic (public API list price reference): ~$24 / 1M tokens
- Typical open-host managed (third-party hosting of open models, multi-tenant): ~$10–$18 / 1M depending on model and SLA
- Redwood Hosted (metered, no commit): ~$11 / 1M (standard tier, includes observability + rate limits)
- Redwood Dedicated (12mo commit, reserved capacity + predictability): ~$6–$8 / 1M (dependent on commit size and traffic profile)
- Redwood Private / VPC (on-prem or customer-managed infra + 12mo platform agreement): ~$4–$6 / 1M with hardware commitments and long-term support; requires OPEX/CapEx alignment

Interpretation: your $5–$7 / 1M aspiration is within range if BrightLeaf can commit to a 12mo reserved tier and accept the Private/Dedicated tradeoffs (longer lead time for capacity and some network/inventory constraints). The biggest delta vs public hosts is achieved through Dedicated pooling + caching and the ability to tune quantization for your workload.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to share a one-page pricing term sheet (I attached a mutual-action-plan-draft.docx) that maps commit bands (e.g., 500M, 1.2B, 2.5B tokens) to the committed $/1M tiers above.
2) Schedule a 45-min sync with your procurement + infra leads to review SLOs and the PO template (can be next Tue/Wed).
3) If you want, we can run a short engineering proof-of-cost: 1 week of shadow traffic on a Dedicated pool to validate the $/1M outcome (requires a light traffic mirror and your sign-off).

I'll follow up with the one-page term sheet and a calendar invite for potential slots.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
